entries.text: Roles now belong to a place. Someone can be Supervisor in one department and Staff in another, and what they may do in a project follows their role in that project's department.

There is no department manager. A manager leads whole divisions; adding them to a department in their own division is refused, and adding them to a department in another division asks whether they join as Staff or Supervisor there.
Organization board: the Levels row lists everyone by their highest role in a scrollable box. Drag people from it into a place. Only Director takes drops, since it is the one level without a place.

Organization board: dragging from People adds someone; dragging inside the structure moves them, also between a department and a division. Dragging a division manager from the structure into one of their own departments steps them down to that role. Drag a director from the Director lane back to People to make them Staff.

Organization board layout: the People panel stays in view while you scroll, managers are listed like supervisors and staff, department cards are flatter, and there is a New division button at the end of the list.

The member editor no longer has Other project access or Supervised divisions. Access comes from placements; directors and Super Admins see everything by rule. The editor shows each placement and role read-only; change them on the Organization board.
Chat messages can be pinned. Pinned messages sit in a bar at the top of the conversation; click it to jump to the message.
Copy a chat message's text from its action menu.
Quick reactions on chat messages, plus a + button to pick any other emoji. On touch screens, long-press a message.

Mention more than people. In chat, descriptions and comments, type @ for people, yourself or @all, and # for channels and work items. Empty text fields show the hint @ mention · # channel or work item.
A private channel mentioned in a message shows as "Private channel" to anyone who isn't a member, so its name stays private.
Hover a mention of a person, channel or work item to see a quick preview: the profile card, the channel topic and member count, or the work item's status, priority, due date and assignees.
Images in chat open in the same full-screen viewer as work items, with zoom, instead of a new tab.
Links and images written in a work item's description or comments now also appear under Links and Attachments, marked with where they came from.
Links show a preview card with the page title, summary and image, in descriptions, comments and chat, including while you type a chat message.
Some entries in Your Work activity showed only a name and a time. Every entry now says what changed.
The God Mode audit log showed a blank object type for settings changes. Every God Mode change is now logged with a type and a name.
Mention emails for a work item description could go to the wrong person.
The profile card no longer prints "Division" and "Department" labels next to each unit; the building icon already says it.
Projects are now called departments everywhere. Each department already had exactly one project behind it, so nothing moves; only the word changes.
You can no longer create a project from the app. Create a department in God Mode and its workspace is made for you.

The Wiki is its own space now, not a project. Every division and department has its own folder, created and named from the organization structure. All existing folders and materials were moved over and keep their links.

Who can upload to the Wiki follows your placement: your department, your division if you lead it, everywhere for directors, and General for everyone. Nobody needs to be added to a Wiki project anymore.
Wiki trash: restore deleted folders and materials from the Trash button in the Wiki header.
Labels no longer use all capital letters, and department cards on the Organization board no longer repeat the department name as a project.
